messages:
Sam C.: quick flag — FastPay onboarding hit intermittent 429s during SDK warmup, started ~09:12 UTC. Only on embeddings and reranking. small percentage of requests succeed, others get 429. sample from their worker logs:
```2027-06-10T09:12:34Z ERROR request_id=abc123 status=429 route=/v1/embeddings msg=\"rate_limit\" quota_remaining=0
2027-06-10T09:12:35Z INFO request_id=abc124 status=200 route=/v1/chat```

Sam C.: they said they didn't change traffic pattern — just running SDK with default concurrency. customer is worried about renewal if onboarding stalls.

Devon R.: thanks Sam. couple quick asks: can they paste the SDK config (maxConcurrency / retries)? also request ids help. are they using a short-lived token or API key?

Sam C.: pasted config from customer: `client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_TOKEN, maxConcurrency: 50, retry: { attempts: 3 } })`

Devon R.: ah — two notes: 1) env var name mismatch (we expect REDWOOD_API_KEY but SDK accepts either, might be fine) 2) maxConcurrency=50 is high for initial warmup on Dedicated — causes bursty fanout to proxy -> some upstream rate controllers hit auth throttle. try lowering to 8-12 and enable expo backoff. e.g.:
```js
const client = new Redwood({
  apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY,
  maxConcurrency: 10,
  retry: { strategy: 'exponential', baseDelayMs: 100, maxAttempts: 5 }
})
```

integrations-bot: [alert] spike detected: service=fastpay env=prod metric=auth.throttle count=324 window=5m (link: https://internal/alerts/3421)

Maya (CSM): looping in infra — FastPay is sensitive to latency, they prefer embeddings to be reliable. also they rotate keys daily for security. could rotation be overlapping with warmup?

Oliver I.: looking at proxy traces — we saw many auth cache misses during that window. TL;DR: token rotation + high concurrency caused repeated auth validation calls and bumped them into secondary rate tiers. patch: increase token cache TTL on the proxy from 10s -> 60s for onboarding keys, and ensure stale tokens are validated async.

Devon R.: good catch. additional suggestion: set per-operation concurrency limits (embeddings lower) and add jitter to retries. sample pseudo-config:
```json
{
  "routes": {
    "/v1/embeddings": { "maxConcurrency": 8 },
    "/v1/chat": { "maxConcurrency": 20 }
  },
  "retries": { "strategy": "exponential_jitter", "baseMs": 120 }
}
```

Sam C.: customer tried lowering to 12 and enabled expo backoff. they also created a per-service key (limited scope) to avoid rotation conflict. saw immediate drop in 429s. small sample after change:
```2027-06-10T09:20:12Z INFO request_id=abc500 status=200 route=/v1/embeddings
2027-06-10T09:20:13Z INFO request_id=abc501 status=200 route=/v1/embeddings
```

Maya (CSM): phew :) can we document this as an onboarding best-practice? note: reduce initial concurrency, use scoped service keys during rotation, enable expo_jitter. I'll add to the enablement checklist.

Oliver I.: infra will make token cache TTL configurable per-tenant for onboarding windows. I'll file infra ticket INF-872 and target a patch tomorrow.

Devon R.: I'll add example configs to our SDK quickstart and a short note about token rotation. PR after lunch.

Sam C.: customer is unblocked and we scheduled a 15m follow-up to validate continued stability. thanks all :thumbsup:

Maya (CSM): action items:
- Maya: update enablement checklist with fix steps
- Devon: SDK quickstart examples + retry defaults
- Oliver: infra ticket INF-872 (token cache TTL per-tenant)
- Sam: confirm renewal health check next week

Sam C.: adding screenshots and request ids to the ticket. closing thread for now, will reopen if it resurfaces.
